newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul mulls upping foreign shr holding over 23 pct.
newsitem.headline: Seoul mulls upping foreign shr holding over 23 pct.

text.p: South Korea's Finance and Economic Ministry is considering expanding the foreign stock ownership limit to above the earlier planned 23 percent in 1997, a ministry official said on Monday.
"We are studying various ways to expand the ceiling to 25-26 percent over two occasions this year," the official said by telephone.
The ministry had earlier said South Korea planned to raise the foreign stock holding limit to 23 percent this year and 26 percent next year.
At present, foreign investors can buy up to 20 percent in a single company listed on the local bourse.
The official said the government would take into account "factors other than the stock market" when it decides on the expansion of the foreign shareholding limit. He gave no other details.
The government has tried to take steps to promote the inflow of foreign funds to help stop the local currency from losing its value rapidly.

With South Korea's current account deficit hitting records, the won, quoted at 879.50 to the dollar on Monday, has lost 11.91 percent against the U.S. dollar since the begining of last year. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5647
